newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Merchant Bank in venture for plantation.
newsitem.headline: Merchant Bank in venture for plantation.

text.p: Merchant Bank of Sri Lanka and two Sri Lankan investors have formed a joint venture to buy controlling stakes in estate firms which are being privatised, the venture said on Friday.
The other partners of the venture, called Plantation Investment & Management Co Ltd (PIMC), are the state-owned Sri Lanka Insurance Corporation and Employees Trust Fund (ETF), a PIMC statement said.
"PIMC has been incorported to acquire controlling interest of a few potentially resourceful and profitable regional plantation companies," it said.
PIMC will also seek listing on the Colombo Stock Exchange "within a relatively short time".
Participants of the venture said they were motivated mainly by the need for medium to long-term investment.
"We are there purely as a viable investment for our long-term life funds," said Jagath Wickremasinghe, chairman of Sri Lanka Insurance.
ETF, funded by employer contributions on behalf of employees, is also attracted by the medium to long-term nature of the investment, said its chairman Denzil Gunaratne.
Sri Lanka began privatising 23 plantation companies which own tea, rubber and coconut estates, in late 1995.
Six of them are now trading on the stock exchange.
PIMC has so far bought 51 percent in Hapugastenne Plantations Ltd, which was privatised by selling 51 percent on the stock exchange in late August.
Analysts believe the company could bid for a further two plantation firms.
